approvals.approval: Place of Entertainment, Limited Live Performance or Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit

basis.text: A live performance, a DJ or karaoke needs a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (one performer without amplification who ends by 10 p.m. needs none). Regular amplified sound outdoors needs a Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit. The Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on each application. Recorded music indoors with no performer needs no entertainment permit, and dancing by patrons needs no permit of its own. Where a permit is needed: further review.
basis.code_section: San Francisco Police Code § 1060 et seq. (Place of Entertainment; Limited Live Performance; Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound)

referral_steps.text: Place of Entertainment Permit application: this application is sent to the Police Department for review (Police Code § 1060.2(b)(1); § 1060.5(a)).

filing_playbook.action: Identify and secure a commitment from another bar within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD to transfer their ABC Type 42 license to 995 Valencia St; confirm the source bar's address, license number and that the license is in good standing.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Contact bars within the Mission SUD (bounded roughly by 16th St, Potrero Ave, Cesar Chavez St, and Dolores St) to negotiate the purchase and transfer of their Type 42 license; engage a license broker if needed. Obtain a signed letter of intent or purchase agreement stating the source bar's address, ABC license number, and the transfer terms. ABC and Planning will ask for this documentation in the CUA and ABC transfer applications.

filing_playbook.action: Once the CUA is approved by the Planning Commission, file the ABC Type 42 application with the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Budget 60–150 days for the transfer if unprotested.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Before the DPH pre-opening inspection, obtain a Certified Food Protection Manager certificate (ServSafe or equivalent) for at least one owner or employee, and ensure all food-handling employees complete the California Food Handler Card course.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register for a ServSafe or Prometric food safety manager exam ($100–$250, 1–14 days to schedule and receive results) and pass the exam; DPH asks for the certificate at the pre-opening inspection. All employees who handle food must obtain a California Food Handler Card from an ANSI-accredited provider within 30 days of hire ($7–$15, online course takes about two hours, valid 3 years).
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Before opening, register all alcohol servers and managers for California RBS (Responsible Beverage Service) training, subscribe to ASCAP and BMI music licenses, and set up workers' compensation insurance and EDD employer registration.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: All alcohol servers and managers must complete RBS certification within 60 days of hire: register on the ABC RBS Portal ($3), complete an approved course ($10–$25), pass the exam, and keep the certification list on site. Subscribe to ASCAP and BMI blanket licenses for live and recorded music (formula-based fees, typically $300–$2,500/year each). Obtain workers' compensation insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund (premiums are 2–6% of payroll for restaurant class codes, no government fee); the health and entertainment permits ask for proof of coverage. Register as an employer with EDD within 15 days of paying wages (free, online, 1–7 days).

timeline_cost.notes: The day range (120–300 days) and cost range ($6,278–$21,100 in government and application fees) cover the time and fees to obtain the four approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000 per the catalog), Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (45–120 days, $2,708–$3,800), Health Permit to Operate (14–45 days, $470–$1,000), and Building Permit with change of use (14–120 days, $800–$15,000). The CUA timeline is the critical path and runs in parallel with the Entertainment Commission permit; the ABC Type 42 license transfer (60–150 days, $1,000–$1,600) begins after CUA approval and runs in parallel with building construction, so it is not added to the day range but its fee is included in a separate alcohol-license line item. The ranges assume the CUA is approved and no appeal is filed; a denial, withdrawal or appeal adds months and is not a time to approval. The cost range includes only government fees and permit application fees; it does not include the cost to purchase the Type 42 license from the source bar (market price, typically $5,000–$50,000+ depending on seller and negotiation), architect and engineering fees for plans ($10,000–$30,000+), construction costs ($50,000–$150,000+ for kitchen, bar, finishes and ADA upgrades), license broker fees (10–15% of license purchase price if used), or legal counsel. ABC's undue-concentration test for census tract 208.01 (28 licenses against 12 authorized) may trigger a Public Convenience or Necessity hearing before the Board of Supervisors, adding 2–4 months; confirm the PCN requirement with SF Planning's ABC liaison before filing.
